reason: The text demonstrates the opposite of the stated claim. The entire narrative of Jonah illustrates God's willingness to show mercy and compassion toward even a foreign people (Nineveh). When the Ninevites repent, God explicitly relents from the disaster He planned to bring upon them (3:10). In the final passage (4:10-11), God explains His compassion to Jonah: 'I—shall I not have compassion on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know between their right hand and their left, and many animals?' This demonstrates both loyalty through mercy and deep care for the people. Moreover, there is no mention anywhere in this text of God considering replacing any people with another people. The narrative focuses on God's character as merciful, compassionate, and unwilling to destroy the repentant.
